hardware.title: Hardware
hardware.no_fix: No position fix yet, so there is nothing to publish. Turn Coverage on again once the device knows where it is.
hardware.intro: What this device is made of. Other nodes use it to decide who to ask for what — and on the day the grid goes down, a machine that is still running matters more than a fast one that is not.
hardware.powered.unwatched: Not watched long enough to say — and an honest "I don't know" beats a guess another node would rank us on.
hardware.powered.measured: Measured here, one sample an hour. This is what other nodes are told; they weigh what they have seen of us above anything we claim.
hardware.uplink.label: How this device reaches the world
hardware.speed.why: Satellite looks exactly like ordinary Wi-Fi from in here, and that difference is the whole point of the field — so if this runs on Starlink, say so.
hardware.coverage.title: Say where this device serves
hardware.coverage.off: Off — it says nothing about where it is
hardware.coverage.precision: Precision — this is what the network is told, and nothing finer. The fine digits are never stored, so they cannot leak later.
hardware.coverage.phone: A phone should leave this off: a device in your pocket has no business advertising where it sleeps. Turn it on for a gateway on a hill or a box in a village hall — being found is the whole reason it is up there.
hardware.radios.intro: One row per antenna. A machine with a LoRa hat and a VHF rig has two very different footprints, and one number would lie about both. The frequency is what makes the range usable: a range says a station could hear you, a frequency says where to call.
hardware.verdict.normal.fast: On a normal day this is a useful, fast node.
hardware.verdict.normal.phone: On a normal day this is an ordinary phone: it reads and posts, and it serves strangers nothing on a metered plan.
hardware.verdict.normal.plain: On a normal day this is an ordinary node.
hardware.verdict.best: If the grid goes down it becomes one of the most valuable nodes your network has: still powered, a path out that no local infrastructure can take away, and reachable over the air by people with no signal at all. Keep it running.
hardware.verdict.offgrid: If the grid goes down it keeps working and stays reachable over the air — which is exactly when a neighbourhood needs a node like this one.
hardware.verdict.power: It survives a power cut. Adding a LoRa antenna would make it reachable when the internet goes too.
hardware.verdict.reach: It can be reached without the internet, but it dies with the grid. A battery or a panel would change that.
hardware.verdict.depends: It depends on the grid and on somebody else's network. That is fine — most devices do, and the mesh is built out of them.
hardware.radio.range.help: How far it really reaches. You know; no API does.
hardware.schedule.duty: wakes for {awake} every {period} ({pct}% of the time)
